profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting at a quantitative asset management firm evaluating whether an internal adaptation of a Reinforced Deep Markov Model (RDMM) for optimal execution is ready to move from research prototype to a controlled paper-trading pilot. The research pod has reproduced promising results on historical limit order book data for Meta, Intel, Vodafone, and Microsoft, and prepared a review package covering the latent-state architecture, ablation studies, execution simulation, and a pilot requirements document. The agenda is to assess whether the current design package is sufficient for conditional approval, identify any gaps in the supporting evidence, and agree on what revisions are needed before the model can enter the firm's paper-trading workflow. The expected outcome is a decision on whether the RDMM can proceed with only documentation updates or whether additional design evidence is required.

members.name: Maya Chen
members.expertise: Model-based reinforcement learning, market microstructure modeling, and experimental design for trading systems
members.background: Maya leads the firm's execution research pod and adapted the RDMM architecture from academic work into the firm's internal research stack, including latent-state filtering, uncertainty-aware planning, and historical execution simulations.
members.private_state: She wants the review to end with a light conditional approval because engineering time for the paper-trading harness has already been reserved next sprint, and she is trying to avoid reopening the research package with additional bespoke analyses.
hidden_assumptions: The pilot requirements document for a research-controlled paper-trading phase is mainly a concise summary of model purpose, offline evidence, and integration dependencies, with links to standard controls added later by platform teams.

The 'execution simulator' in this package is naturally understood to be the firm's historical replay simulator with calibrated temporary and permanent impact overlays, because that is the standard tool used by the execution research pod.

When people mention 'stress scenarios' in an execution-model review, they mean difficult market regimes such as earnings days, volatile opens and closes, and spread-widening intervals in the historical data.

An ablation section is complete if each major RDMM component is removed one at a time and the effects are shown on the main study universe at aggregate level; symbol-level breakdowns are supplementary unless a failure is already suspected.

If the pilot is shadow-only and manually supervised each day, the design review does not need to spell out control templates in detail because those are inherited from the existing paper-trading process.

members.name: Daniel Ortiz
members.role: Model Risk and Trading Controls Reviewer
members.expertise: Model governance, algorithmic trading controls, validation standards, and execution platform rollout reviews
members.background: Daniel sits in the model risk group and reviews new trading models before they can be exercised in any live decision workflow, including shadow and paper-trading modes connected to the firm's execution platform.
members.private_state: He wants to be constructive and avoid sounding like a blocker, but a recent internal audit criticized ambiguous handoffs between research packages and pilot approvals, so he is quietly looking for evidence that the documentation already maps cleanly into the firm's governance templates.
hidden_assumptions: A pilot requirements document is the review artifact that should already anchor the standard paper-trading control template, even if some fields are filled by engineering later.

The 'execution simulator' cited in a design review should be interpreted as a venue-aware simulator that preserves queue position and fill mechanics closely enough to support claims about action-dependent market effects.

When someone says 'stress scenarios,' they are referring to the model-risk scenario library that includes feed dropouts, halts, crossed books, stale quotes, and thin-depth conditions in addition to volatile market periods.
Ablation evidence is only decision-useful if it can reveal where the model's contribution varies by instrument or market structure, especially across names as different as Vodafone and Microsoft.
If a model is entering the paper-trading workflow, the review package is expected to align with existing governance artifacts rather than treating those artifacts as a separate downstream step.

misalignment_points.topic: What the 'pilot requirements document' is supposed to contain
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to updating or reviewing the 'pilot requirements document'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya treats it as a research-facing summary document that explains the RDMM design, validation results, and integration needs before shadow deployment.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes it is the initiating artifact for the firm's standard paper-trading governance package and therefore should already connect to control fields, monitoring hooks, and exception ownership.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The document name sounds formal and shared, and both have seen similarly titled artifacts before; because neither wants to derail the meeting into process minutiae, they speak as if the document's function is obvious.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss validating the RDMM in the 'execution simulator'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya means the firm's historical replay simulator with slippage plus calibrated impact overlays derived from prior execution studies.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means a higher-fidelity queue-aware simulation environment that approximates venue matching, fill uncertainty, and order-book position effects.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase is standard shorthand inside the firm and both tools plausibly fit under it; because the meeting is nominally about design sufficiency rather than simulator implementation, the fidelity gap stays hidden.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a complete 'ablation package'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the ablation package should be 'complete enough' for review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya believes completeness means each major RDMM block has been toggled off separately and the aggregate performance impact is reported across the main four-symbol study set.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel believes completeness requires enough disaggregation to show whether the claimed benefit holds consistently across materially different symbols, not just in the pooled average.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Ablation methodology sounds like a technical detail already handled by the research team, so Daniel asks about completeness at a high level while Maya answers with confidence using a different standard of sufficiency.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both mention that the RDMM has been checked against 'the stress scenarios'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya is thinking of the research team's difficult trading windows: earnings days, volatile opens and closes, abrupt spread widening, and noisy book periods in the historical sample.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is thinking of the model-risk scenario set: exchange halts, data-feed interruptions, stale or crossed books, and unusually sparse depth conditions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each function uses the plural phrase as if it names a single familiar package, and both sets are genuinely relevant to 'stress'; the overlap in wording makes the mismatch feel too trivial to question.

turns.inner_thought: I want this to end with a light conditional approval and nothing that reopens the research package. Engineering already has paper-trading harness time blocked next sprint. The pilot requirements document should be treated as the research-facing summary: purpose, offline evidence, and integration dependencies. The standard controls can be layered in later through the existing paper-trading process.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making the time. The goal from my side is to confirm the RDMM package is ready for conditional approval. I updated the pilot requirements document alongside the offline results, so I’m hoping we can focus on whether there’s anything material still missing before it moves into the paper-trading workflow.

turns.inner_thought: Good, she has updated the pilot requirements document. After the audit comments, I need to see that this artifact already anchors the paper-trading governance path, not just the research story. I don't want to sound like a blocker, but I need enough in there that the standard controls, monitoring hooks, and ownership can map in cleanly.
turns.utterance: That’s helpful. Could you walk me through the pilot requirements document from the standpoint of what the paper-trading review will lean on? I mainly want to understand whether the handoff is already structured cleanly.

turns.inner_thought: He wants the usual package overview. I’ll keep it at the level of objective, architecture, evidence, and dependencies. For me the key validation is that the latent-state model and uncertainty-aware planner worked in our historical replay execution simulator with calibrated temporary and permanent impact overlays across Meta, Intel, Vodafone, and Microsoft.
turns.utterance: Sure. It starts with the model objective and decision scope, then gives the architecture summary, the main offline findings, and the integration dependencies. We validated the full RDMM in the execution simulator across Meta, Intel, Vodafone, and Microsoft, against the current schedule-style baselines, and I also noted the supervision model we’d use during the pilot.

turns.inner_thought: Using the execution simulator is the right basis. What I need to infer is whether the action-dependent behavior still looks sensible when queue conditions deteriorate and fills become less certain. If their execution simulator covered that sort of venue behavior, the claims are much easier to carry into review.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. On the execution simulator side, did the action-dependent behavior stay stable when market conditions got less forgiving? That’s usually where I get the clearest read on whether the policy is behaving consistently.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, especially in the difficult historical windows we always use: earnings days, volatile opens and closes, spread widening, noisy book periods. The latent filter helped most in those regimes. I’ll frame it in terms of the stress scenarios and keep it moving.
turns.utterance: Yes, that was actually one of the stronger parts of the package. The model looked most robust in the stress scenarios, especially in the periods where the market was moving around more aggressively, and that was where the filtering and uncertainty handling seemed to help the most.

turns.inner_thought: Good to hear they checked the stress scenarios. I still need to know whether that includes the usual scenario-library edge cases I think of—feed issues, stale or crossed books, thin depth, halts—but I can ask more softly so I don't derail the meeting.
turns.utterance: That’s reassuring. And just so I place it correctly, did the stress scenarios also include the more extreme edge cases you’d normally expect to see covered at this stage?

turns.inner_thought: Yes, we covered the difficult regimes we care about in the historical sample. I can summarize those windows more explicitly if needed. Better to pivot now to the ablations and show the package is already complete enough: remove latent state, remove uncertainty term, simplify the planner, and report the aggregate effect over the main universe.
turns.utterance: They covered the key difficult cases we wanted to exercise, and I can make that a bit more explicit in the write-up. The other piece worth calling out is the ablation section, because I think that package is complete enough for review: it isolates the contribution of the latent-state block, the uncertainty term, and the planner updates.

turns.inner_thought: Complete enough is exactly the issue. For me that means I can tell whether the claimed benefit is stable across materially different instruments and market structures, not just in a pooled average. I should ask about stability across the test universe without spelling out symbol-level detail.
turns.utterance: That was one of the things I wanted to understand. When you say complete enough, does the ablation package give a clear view of how stable those gains are across the test universe, rather than just at the headline level?

turns.inner_thought: Yes, the pooled results already show the direction is stable across the main four-symbol set, and that should be enough for design review. If he wants a little more visibility, I can add appendix tables, but I don’t want this to turn into bespoke instrument-by-instrument analysis.
turns.utterance: Yes, that’s how we approached it. The main deck emphasizes the top-line picture because the direction is consistent, and if it helps the review I can add a bit more supporting detail in the appendix without changing the core readout.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds workable. If the appendix makes the evidence easier to trace, then the pilot requirements document can probably serve as the initiating artifact for the paper-trading package. I want to keep this constructive and avoid a hard stop.
turns.utterance: Yes, I think that would help. If those additions are folded in, the pilot requirements document should probably be enough for the paper-trading package to move forward, assuming the references are easy to follow.

turns.inner_thought: Good, this is still in documentation-update territory. I can expand the pilot requirements document with a short appendix on the execution simulator and a section on the stress scenarios from the review deck. That should satisfy him without reopening the experimental plan.
turns.utterance: That sounds reasonable. I can expand the document with a short appendix on the execution simulator and add a section that summarizes the stress scenarios already covered in the review deck, along with the supporting ablation material.

turns.inner_thought: Broadly this is enough for me if the revised package makes the simulator support, scenario coverage, and evidence trail explicit inside the pilot requirements document. Then I can support conditional approval and show the handoff is anchored properly.
turns.utterance: Great. With those pieces made explicit, I’m broadly comfortable. If the revised package spells that out clearly, I think the design can proceed toward conditional approval.
